name: Kentucky

program.agency: Public Protection Cabinet, Office of Claims and Appeals, Crime Victims Compensation Board

sources.title: 802 KAR 3:020 Payment schedule for sexual assault examinations
Crime Victims Compensation Board FAQ (updated August 2024)

rules.summary: When a sexual assault exam is given, no hospital, exam facility, clinician, pharmacist, health department, the survivor's insurer, or the state may charge the survivor for the exam, even if the exam is not completed.
rules.quote: When an examination of a victim of a sexual offense is provided in accordance with this section, no charge shall be made to the victim by the hospital, the sexual assault examination facility, the physician, the pharmacist, the health department, the sexual assault nurse examiner, other qualified medical professional, the victim's insurance carrier, or the Commonwealth for: (a) Sexual assault examinations, whether or not the exam is completed;

rules.summary: The no-charge rule also covers preventive medication, strangulation assessments, and other tests or services tied to the assault or exam on the same date as the exam, including triage and ambulance costs.
rules.quote: (b) Prophylactic medical treatment; (c) Strangulation assessments; or (d) Other medical tests or services, including triage and ambulance expenses, related to the incident, exam, or treatment which occur on the same date as the original exam.

rules.summary: A survivor cannot be refused an exam or billed for it because they choose not to file a police report, cooperate with law enforcement, or take part in the criminal case.
rules.quote: No victim shall be denied an examination, or billed in violation of subsection (10) of this section, because the victim chooses not to file a police report, cooperate with law enforcement, or otherwise participate in the criminal justice system.

rules.summary: The exam program's FAQ says providers should bill the patient's Medicaid or private insurance first, but may not charge a co-pay or deductible.
rules.quote: If a patient has insurance, whether Medicaid or Private insurance, that insurance should be billed first before billing the SAEP, but no co-pay or deductible may be charged as a condition for payment.
rules.pinpoint: SAEP FAQ, "Can we bill the patient's Insurance?"

params.payer: Crime Victims Compensation Board (Sexual Assault Examination Program), paid to the provider

rules.summary: The Crime Victims Compensation Board pays for sexual assault exams and the related no-charge services, at rates set by its regulation.
rules.quote: The examinations provided in accordance with this section and other services provided to a victim pursuant to subsection (10) of this section shall be paid for by the Crime Victims Compensation Board at a rate to be determined by the administrative regulation promulgated by the board

rules.summary: The total award for a claimant cannot exceed $50,000.
rules.quote: Any award made under KRS 49.270 to 49.490 shall not exceed fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) in total compensation to be received by or paid on behalf of a claimant from the fund.

rules.summary: Lost earnings or lost support are paid at net earnings, up to $500 for each week.
rules.quote: the award shall be equal to net earnings at the time of the criminally injurious conduct; however, no award under this subsection shall exceed five hundred dollars ($500) for each week of lost earnings or financial support.

rules.summary: When the crime happened at the victim's home, moving to a new primary residence for safety within 6 months of the crime is covered up to $2,000. The board may allow relocation costs incurred after 6 months at its discretion.
rules.quote: For the victim and for any child who is the victim's dependent, when the crime was committed at the primary residence of the victim: a. Relocation if the victim is moving from one (1) primary residence to another due to concern for the safety of themselves or other persons at the residence as a result of a crime within six (6) months of the crime, not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000). The board may, in its discretion, allow relocation expenses incurred after six (6) months

rules.summary: Temporary housing within 30 days of the crime, when the victim cannot stay at home because of the crime, is covered up to $2,000 (this applies when the crime happened at the victim's home).
rules.quote: Temporary housing costs incurred within thirty (30) days of the crime, when the victim is unable to stay in the primary residence due to the crime, not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000);

rules.summary: Replacing or repairing windows and locks at the victim's home or business damaged in the crime is covered up to $1,500.
rules.quote: Replacement or repair of windows and locks at the primary residence or business of the victim which were damaged by the commission of the crime, not to exceed one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500);

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup within 30 days at the victim's home or business is covered up to $2,000.
rules.quote: Crime scene cleanup within thirty (30) days of the crime when the crime was committed at the primary residence or business of the victim, not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000);

rules.summary: Funeral and burial costs cannot exceed $10,000.
rules.quote: In no event shall an award for funeral expenses exceed ten thousand dollars ($10,000).

rules.summary: Mental health counseling needed because of the crime is covered for up to two years, after proper documentation is submitted to the board. There is no separate dollar cap; it counts toward the overall cap.
rules.quote: Mental health counseling, necessary as a result of the injury upon which the claim is based. Mental health counseling: a. Shall be paid for a maximum of two (2) years, but only after proper documentation is submitted to the board

rules.summary: Awards cover out-of-pocket expenses, including lost earnings or support and debts reasonably incurred for medical or other services.
rules.quote: Any award made pursuant to KRS 49.270 to 49.490 shall be in an amount not exceeding out-of-pocket expenses, including loss of earnings or support resulting from the injury on which the claim is based and indebtedness reasonably incurred for medical or other services

rules.summary: The program lists medical and dental expenses as compensable.
rules.quote: Medical/dental expenses;
rules.pinpoint: CVCB FAQ, "What categories of expenses are compensable by the Board?"

rules.summary: Items seized by police as evidence can be replaced, up to $500 per item.
rules.quote: Reimbursement for the replacement of items owned by the victim and for any child who is the victim's dependent that were seized by law enforcement as evidence of the commission of the crime, not to exceed five hundred dollars ($500) per item;

rules.summary: Replacing eyeglasses or other corrective lenses stolen, destroyed, or damaged in the crime is covered.
rules.quote: Replacement of eyeglasses and other corrective lenses stolen, destroyed, or damaged during the crime.

rules.summary: Rehabilitative or wellness practices recommended by a healthcare provider are covered up to $1,000 per year per person, for at most 2 years.
rules.quote: Rehabilitative or wellness practices recommended by a healthcare provider, engaged in by the victim and any juveniles dependent upon the victim due to the crime, not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000) per year per person, for a maximum of two (2) years;

rules.summary: Travel, parking, lodging, and meals for attending criminal court proceedings related to the crime can be covered for the victim and the victim's caregiver.
rules.quote: A victim and the victim's caregiver, if applicable, may recover the following types of expenses incurred for purposes of attending criminal court proceedings related to the crime: (1) Travel; (2) Parking; (3) Lodging; (4) Meals;

rules.summary: If a claim is filed more than 10 years after the crime because testing or DNA matching of a sexual assault kit was delayed, the victim may collect a $5,000 lump sum for out-of-pocket costs that cannot be proven because of the delay.
rules.quote: An award may be made for a claim filed more than ten (10) years after the criminally injurious conduct, due to a delay in the testing of or DNA profile matching from a sexual assault forensic examination kit or biological material collected as evidence related to a sexual offense, in which case the victim may collect a lump sum in the amount of five thousand dollars ($5,000)

params.item: property loss or damage (for example a stolen or broken phone), unless the statute allows it, such as items seized as evidence or windows and locks

rules.summary: No award is made for property loss or damage, such as a phone, except where the statute allows it (for example, items seized by police as evidence, or windows and locks).
rules.quote: An award shall not be made for any type of property loss or damage, except as otherwise permitted in KRS 49.270 to 49.490.

params.item: pain and suffering, emotional distress, loss of consortium

rules.summary: The program does not pay for pain and suffering, emotional distress, or loss of consortium.
rules.quote: Property damage or loss, except as provided in KRS Chapter 49, and pain and suffering, emotional distress, and loss of consortium.
rules.pinpoint: CVCB FAQ, "What types of expenses are NOT compensable by the Board?"

rules.summary: Awards are reduced by money received or to be received from the offender, required insurance, public funds, the claimant's own insurance, an emergency award, or donations toward crime expenses.
rules.quote: Any award made pursuant to KRS 49.270 to 49.490 shall be reduced by the amount of any payments received or to be received by the claimant as a result of the injury from the following sources: (a) From or on behalf of the person who committed the crime; (b) Under insurance programs mandated by law; (c) From public funds; (d) Under any contract of insurance wherein the claimant is the insured or beneficiary; (e) As an emergency award pursuant to KRS 49.360; and (f) From donations made on behalf of the victim or claimant toward expenses incurred as a result of the crime.

rules.summary: The board may deny, reconsider, or reduce an award if the victim or claimant was charged with an offense, was offered immunity, knowingly took part in the conduct, or engaged in mutual aggression, in relation to the crime in the claim.
rules.quote: The board may deny, reconsider, or reduce an award if the board finds that, in relation to the criminally injurious conduct alleged in the claim, the victim or claimant: (a) Has been charged with a criminal offense; (b) Has been offered immunity from prosecution in exchange for testimony; (c) Knowingly participated in the conduct; or (d) Engaged in conduct which may constitute mutual aggression with another person.

rules.summary: An emergency award of up to $1,000 can be paid before the final decision, and it is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: The amount of an emergency award shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000); (b) The amount of an emergency award shall be deducted from any final award made to the claimant;

rules.summary: Compensation covers victims of criminally injurious conduct, meaning conduct in Kentucky that poses a substantial threat of physical or psychological injury and is punishable as a crime.
rules.quote: "Criminally injurious conduct" means conduct that occurs or is attempted in this jurisdiction, poses a substantial threat of personal physical or psychological injury or death, and is punishable by fine, imprisonment, or death.

rules.summary: The official claim form lists adult sexual assault as a crime type.
rules.quote: Sexual Assault (Adult)

params.rule: Victims injured by a criminal act in Kentucky

rules.summary: A victim is a person injured or killed by a criminal act in Kentucky.
rules.quote: "Victim" means a person who suffers personal physical or psychological injury or death from a criminal act in Kentucky as a result of:

params.rule: Nonresidents hurt by crimes in Kentucky, while federal funds are available

rules.summary: Nonresidents who suffer losses from crimes in Kentucky are covered during periods when the board finds federal funds are available.
rules.quote: "Victim" shall also include nonresidents of this state who suffer losses as a direct result of criminal acts occurring within this state. This section shall be operative only during those time periods during which the Crime Victims Compensation Board determines that federal funds are available to the state for the compensation of victims of crime.

params.rule: Kentucky residents victimized in a state with no compensation program

rules.summary: A Kentucky resident hurt by a crime in another state can apply in Kentucky only if that state has no compensation program the victim is eligible for and the crime would be covered had it happened in Kentucky.
rules.quote: "Victim" shall also mean a resident who is a victim of a crime occurring outside this state if: 1. The crime would be compensable had it occurred inside this state; and 2. The crime occurred in a state which does not have a crime victim compensation program, for which the victim is eligible as eligibility is set forth in KRS 49.310.

coverage.notes: Filing deadline and police report rule: 2024 Ky. Acts ch. 67 (SB 319, effective July 15, 2024) deleted the old five-year filing limit from KRS 49.330 and the old 48-hour report rule. The current KRS 49.330 and 49.370 text sets no general filing deadline and no reporting deadline, so no filing_deadline or reporting_requirement rule is recorded. The CVCB FAQ (updated August 2024) still lists a police report of the incident among the documents generally required with a claim, and the claim form asks when and to whom the crime was reported, so a survivor should expect to be asked for one; the program brochure says the sexual assault exam program does not require reporting. No minimum loss amount was found. The program's HTML pages (static_id=158 and 159) could not be saved because the fetch tool strips their ASP.NET form content; their PDFs were saved instead.

researcher_notes: Caps come from KRS 49.370 as amended effective July 15, 2024 and match the CVCB FAQ cap list ($50,000 overall, $500 per week lost earnings, $2,000 relocation, $2,000 temporary housing, $10,000 funeral, $1,000 emergency). Relocation and temporary housing apply only when the crime happened at the victim's primary residence. The SAEP FAQ (revised 11/2023) predates the 2024 and 2025 amendments: its dollar fee schedule (citing 107 KAR 2:010) is superseded by 802 KAR 3:020 Medicaid-rate caps, and its statements that incomplete exams and same-day ambulance or triage are not paid conflict with current KRS 216B.400(10), which bars charging the victim for exams whether or not completed and for same-day triage and ambulance. Only its insurance-billing answer is used (KY-EXAM-4), and that matches the current program web page, which says providers bill insurance first. Under KRS 49.340(4) claims are investigated whether or not the offender is caught, charged, or convicted. Emergency award requests are limited to one per claimant by the program's January 2025 policy (KY-S21). Reviewer note: the live exam program page (static_id=159, read with curl but not saveable by fetch_source.py, which returns blocked or empty even with --chrome) says providers bill private or public insurance first, matching KY-EXAM-4, but it also says the victim may be charged for expenses not related to the exam process such as ambulance and triage. That conflicts with current KRS 216B.400(10)(d), which bars charging the victim for same-day triage and ambulance costs, so the statute (KY-EXAM-2) controls.
